api_01.title: What is an API?
api_01.prompt: An API on the internet works like what?
api_01.explanation: API stands for Application Programming Interface. It's like a digital waiter that fetches data on the internet for your code!
options: A waiter that takes your order to the internet server and brings back the response

api_02.title: JSON Data Format
api_02.prompt: On the internet, data almost always arrives in JSON format, which is very similar to a Python dictionary. Complete to get the status value:
api_02.explanation: JSON is the universal web format for sending and receiving information!

api_03.title: Extracting Weather Temperature
api_03.prompt: Order the code to access the current temperature inside the response from a weather forecast API:
api_03.explanation: Nested dictionaries (one inside another) are super common when receiving real data from the web!

api_04.title: API URL Builder
api_04.prompt: Create a function `construir_url(endpoint, usuario)` that joins a website address with the username: `f"https://api.exemplo.com/{endpoint}/{usuario}"`
api_04.explanation: Building dynamic URLs with f-strings lets us fetch information for any user on the web!

boss_battle_18.title: The Guardian of Networks
boss_battle_18.prompt: Given the response dictionary `api_data = {"user": "Heroi", "score": 999}`, print `"Heroi marcou 999"` using an f-string!
